evidence.quote: It is an existence result for the constructed infinite-range interaction, with no identification of its phases as conventional fluid phases.

exclusions.reason: The theorem is an existence result and does not identify the phases as conventional fluid phases.

hypotheses.statement:
There is a bounded continuous function $\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ and finite constants $B,C>0$ such that $$\sum_{i<j}\phi(\left|x_i-x_j\right|)\ge-BN,
 \qquad
 \left|\phi(r)\right|\le C r^{-3-1/32}\quad(r\ge1).$$ There are an open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ centered at $5p/3$ and a common inverse temperature $\beta_c\in[7/8,9/8]$ such that, for every $\rho\in I$, the canonical free energy $$f(\beta,\rho)=
 -\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac1{\beta L^3}
       \log Z^\phi_{L,\lfloor\rho L^3\rfloor}(\beta)$$ exists and is finite for every $\beta>0$. Its finite one-sided derivatives at $\beta_c$ satisfy $$f'_-(\beta_c,\rho)>f'_+(\beta_c,\rho).$$ In particular, $f(\,\cdot\,,\rho)$ is not differentiable at $\beta_c$.
Let $M_L$ be the maximum cardinality of a subset of $[0,L]^3$ whose distinct points have mutual distances at least one. Then $$p=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{M_L}{L^3}$$ exists and belongs to $(0,\infty)$.
For any finite configuration in $\mathbb R^3$, join two particles when their distance belongs to $I_t$. This graph has no clique of size five. On any $m$ vertices it has at most $3m^2/8$ edges.

Fix $t$ satisfying [f:t-requirements] and a compact $\mathcal D\subset\Omega$. There are constants $C_{\exp},C_1<\infty$, depending only on $t$ and $\mathcal D$, such that every grand canonical measure for an interaction [f:modified-energy] satisfies $$\label{f:moment-estimates} \sup_i\mathbb E\exp(\beta D_0n_i^2/4)\le C_{\exp}, \qquad \sup_{i,j}\mathbb E[n_i n_j]\le C_1 \qquad ((\beta,h)\in\mathcal D).$$ The bounds hold for every bounded region with finitely many cropped cells, and uniformly for all permitted deletions and interpolations.

For a finite or countably infinite member of [f:family], let $$\varphi_k=\psi_t-t\sum_{j\le k}\alpha_jw_{R_j}, \qquad m_k=\sum_{j>k}\alpha_j.$$ For every compact $\mathcal D\subset\Omega$ there is a constant $C_{\mathcal D,t}<\infty$, independent of the ranges, their number, and $k$, such that $$\label{f:tail-pressure-bound} 0\le Q_\varphi(\beta,h)-Q_{\varphi_k}(\beta,h) \le C_{\mathcal D,t}m_k \qquad ((\beta,h)\in\mathcal D).$$ The same upper bound holds for the difference of normalized finite volume log grand partition functions in every cube of side $L\ge1$.

Suppose the size conditions on $t$ in [f:stability](#f:stability) hold, including $ct>4(A+1)$. For every $0[k:transform] are exactly the maximizing densities in [k:density-transform]; in particular, they are nonnegative and form a nonempty compact set. On each compact $\mathcal D\subset\Omega$, they lie in a common interval $[0,U]$, independently of $\varphi$ and $a$. The constant $U$ may also be chosen uniformly for all sufficiently large $t$.* *The function $T_aQ$ is finite and convex on $\Omega$, and $$0\le T_aQ-Q\le C_{\mathcal D}a \qquad\hbox{on }\mathcal D. \label{k:small-mass}$$ Here $C_{\mathcal D}$ can be chosen uniformly for sufficiently large $t$. For fixed $t$, the pressures $Q$ and transforms $T_aQ$ have common bounds on compact subsets of $\Omega$, and common local Lipschitz bounds, uniformly over the same family and masses.

Let $a>0$ be as in [k:transform-properties](#k:transform-properties), and let $u$ be active at $\lambda=(\beta,h)$. Then for every $r\in\mathbb R$, $$Q(x_u+(0,r))\le Q(x_u)+ur+\frac{r^2}{2\beta a}.
 \label{k:parabola}$$ Every member of $\partial Q(x_u)$ has second coordinate $u$.

For each fixed $0<a\le2(A+1)$ and $\lambda=(\beta,h)\in\Omega$, $$\partial(T_aQ)(\lambda)
 =\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}\!\bigcup_{u\text{ active at }\lambda}
 \left\{\left(e+\frac a2u^2,u\right):(e,u)\in\partial Q(x_u)\right\}.
 \label{k:support-hull}$$ The union on the right is compact, and every one of its members is an actual supporting slope of $T_aQ$ at $\lambda$.

Fix an admissible $t$ and a compact set $\mathcal D\subset\Omega$. There are constants $C_{\mathcal D,t}<\infty$ and $K_{\mathcal D,t}<\infty$ with the following property. Let $R_0\ge2$, and let $$\varphi_0=\psi_t-t\sum_j\alpha_jw_{R_j},
 \qquad 1\le R_j\le R_0,
 \qquad \alpha_j\ge0,$$ where the sum may be empty, finite, or countably infinite. If $a>0$, $\sum_j\alpha_j+a\le A+1$, and $R/R_0\ge K_{\mathcal D,t}$, then $$\sup_{\lambda\in\mathcal D}
 \left|Q_{\varphi_0-ta w_R}(\lambda)-T_aQ_{\varphi_0}(\lambda)\right|
 \le C_{\mathcal D,t}\sqrt{\frac{R_0}{R}}.
 \label{k:range-estimate}$$ Both constants are independent of $R_0$, the number and values of the reference ranges, the reference masses, and the positive mass $a$.

Let $B_z$ be the box of side $s$ centered at $z$, where $z$ ranges over a translated lattice $s\mathbb Z^3$, and suppose $0<s\le R$. Define $$K^+_{zz'}=\sup_{x\in B_z,\,y\in B_{z'}}w_R(x-y),
 \qquad
 K^-_{zz'}=\inf_{x\in B_z,\,y\in B_{z'}}w_R(x-y).$$ There is a constant $C_w$ depending only on $w$ and dimension such that, with $\eta=C_ws/R$, every finite cubical collection of these boxes satisfies $$s^3\sum_{z'}K^+_{zz'}\le1+\eta.
 \label{k:upper-row}$$ If $z$ has distance greater than $R+4s$ from the boundary of the finite collection, then $$s^3\sum_{z'\ne z}K^-_{zz'}\ge1-\eta.
 \label{k:lower-row}$$ Both matrices are symmetric and nonnegative.

Let $q^{(t)}=Q_{\psi_t}$, with the pressure normalization and the core of [f:thermodynamics](#f:thermodynamics), [f:core](#f:core). Then, locally uniformly on $\Omega=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, $$q^{(t)}(\beta,h)\longrightarrow
 q_*(\beta,h):=\max\{0,ph,4ph-9p\}.
 \label{i:bare-limit}$$

There are constants $0<\tau<p/16$ and $\gamma>0$ with the following properties. Every choice $w_i\in\overline B(v_i,\tau)$, $i=1,2,3$, satisfies $$\overline B(g,\gamma)\subset\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}.
 \label{i:robust-triangle}$$ For each distinct pair $i,j$, $$g\notin\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}\bigl(\overline B(v_i,\tau)\cup\overline B(v_j,\tau)\bigr).
 \label{i:two-groups}$$ Moreover, for every $\lambda\in\Omega$, $$P_*(\lambda)-P_*(\lambda_*)
       -\left\langle g,\lambda-\lambda_*\right\rangle
 \ge\gamma\left\lVert\lambda-\lambda_*\right\rVert.
 \label{i:linear-growth}$$

For all sufficiently large finite $t$, the size conditions in [f:stability](#f:stability), [k:transform-properties](#k:transform-properties) hold and $$\sup_{\lambda\in W_1}\left|P_1^t(\lambda)-P_*(\lambda)\right|
       <\frac{\gamma}{64}.
 \label{i:initial-pressure-error}$$ At every $\lambda\in W_1$ one also has the exact identity $$\partial P_1^t(\lambda)
 =\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}\left(
       \partial P_1^t(\lambda)\cap
       \bigcup_{i=1}^3\overline B(v_i,\tau/2)\right).
 \label{i:initial-hull}$$ Fix one such $t$ for the rest of the construction.

For every $n\ge1$ and $y\in W_n$, $$\label{eq:separated-generators}
 \partial P_n(y)=
 \mathop{\mathrm{conv}}\left(\partial P_n(y)\cap
                 \bigcup_{i=1}^3\overline B(v_i,r_n)\right).$$

For every $n\ge1$, there is $\lambda_n\in\operatorname{int}W(1/8)$ such that $$\label{eq:common-pressure-ball}
 \overline B(g,\gamma)\subset\partial P_n(\lambda_n).$$

Suppose that $H(\beta,d)$ and $Q(\beta,h)$ have the duality and finiteness properties of [f:thermodynamics](#f:thermodynamics); assume also, as there, that $H(\,\cdot\,,d)$ is concave on $(0,\infty)$ for every $d>0$. If $$(s_1,\rho),(s_2,\rho)\in\partial Q(\beta_c,h_c),
 \qquad \rho>0,\quad s_1<s_2,$$ then $H(\,\cdot\,,\rho)$ has finite one-sided derivatives at $\beta_c$ and $$H'_+(\beta_c,\rho)\le-s_2<-s_1\le H'_-(\beta_c,\rho).$$

purpose: A radial continuum phase transition with algebraic decay

coverage.checked_domain: All 1099 labelled graphs on zero through five vertices with no clique of size five, uniform weights; three asymmetric or zero-weight cases; three rejected inputs.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exact Fraction arithmetic rechecks every compressed witness for normalization, clique support, objective monotonicity, the 3/8 bound, and the edge bound. No geometric realization is certified.

coverage.checked_domain: Only the finite graph ingredient is exercised; no continuum integrals, multiscale limits, or derivative jumps are tested.
coverage.oracle_basis: Finite rational witness checking cannot certify the thermodynamic existence theorem.

title: A radial continuum phase transition with algebraic decay
